title: Partial Exits and Weighted R
objective: Apply partial exits and weighted r to a reproducible decision record.
why: Honest measurement prevents outcome bias and unsupported claims.
core: Weight every exit by its fraction of the original quantity. Keep the original risk denominator.
Every example here is original and synthetic. It is not verified historical performance or a trading recommendation.
Arithmetic is illustrative; rules and assessment thresholds are curriculum policy, not evidence of profitable edge.
scenario: A simulated position starts with $100 planned risk. Half exits at +1R and half at +3R. Total costs are $12.
exercise: Compute gross and net R; compare with exiting all at +3R without assuming that target always fills.
quiz: Explain the result and its limitations.
What evidence must remain unknown?
Any execution, cost or timing field not established by the supplied record.
mistake: Treating an attractive chart or small sample as proof of net realized performance.
evidence: Official general risk guidance plus original educational arithmetic and research-design practice; not a validated strategy.

title: Breakeven Is Not Risk-Free
objective: Apply breakeven is not risk-free to a reproducible decision record.
why: Honest measurement prevents outcome bias and unsupported claims.
core: A stop trigger at entry does not guarantee a flat net result. Trailing rules change the payoff distribution and require testing.
Every example here is original and synthetic. It is not verified historical performance or a trading recommendation.
Arithmetic is illustrative; rules and assessment thresholds are curriculum policy, not evidence of profitable edge.
scenario: A simulated long fills at 100 and its stop moves to 100. The exit fills at 99.8; quantity is 50 and total costs are $5.
exercise: Calculate net P/L and explain why moving a stop cannot be called removing all risk.
quiz: Explain the result and its limitations.
(99.8 - 100) x 50 - 5 = -$15. Gaps, slippage and costs remain.

title: Expectancy and Sample Uncertainty
objective: Apply expectancy and sample uncertainty to a reproducible decision record.
why: Honest measurement prevents outcome bias and unsupported claims.
core: Sample mean is an estimate, not proof of future edge. Dependence, changing conditions and selective reporting can invalidate simple confidence arguments.
Every example here is original and synthetic. It is not verified historical performance or a trading recommendation.
Arithmetic is illustrative; rules and assessment thresholds are curriculum policy, not evidence of profitable edge.
scenario: Ten synthetic outcomes contain four +2R wins and six -1R losses before costs. Modeled costs total 1R.
exercise: Compute gross and net mean R. List missing evidence before accepting the strategy.
quiz: Explain the result and its limitations.
(4 x 2 - 6) / 10 = +0.2R gross per trade; (2 - 1) / 10 = +0.1R net. Ten outcomes do not establish a stable edge.
